- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates or misses downward spikes; increase early forecast sensitivity to recent lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00), especially in 30-day horizon — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true outcome if sentiment drops.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts — if forecast is >2.5x recent 7d average, adjust downward by 15–30% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows rapid shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00), model often lags — forecast should adjust upward by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 7d moving average, reduce forecast by 10–20% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
